fruit.summary: Built §9 fruit acquisition as pure integer rules. packages/content/src/fruits: FRUIT_EAT_SECONDS=3 (eatTicks 60), PEDESTALS_PER_FRUIT_KIT=2, FRUIT_KIT_IDS (KIT_IDS minus duelist), zod fruitRulesSchema/validateFruitRules, and kitDescriptions for Duelist/Ember/Smoke with validateKitDescriptions. packages/simulation/src/fruits: createFruitConfig, createFruitState(sites, seed, preset, {tick?, rules?}) with a seeded Fisher-Yates deal (it refuses a wrong site count, duplicate ids and a preset whose fruitKits != 2, so alpha is refused), stepFruits (players sorted by id; channels continue on lastTick+1; results eat-started/interrupted/refused/completed/tick-rejected; completions go to the lowest id and later completers get 'taken'; a stale or repeated tick returns the same state object), kitOf (duelist by default and for unknown ids), inspectPedestal, replayFruits and checkFruitState. Added a ./fruits subpath export to each package.json (source condition first) and docs/fruits.md. Tests: content fruits.test.ts (5), simulation fruits.test.ts (20 scripted: dealing, eating, contests over all 24 permutations, commitment, inspection) and property.test.ts (80 seeds of invariants, EXERCISED over every result kind and reason, replay hash, input-order symmetry). I ran npm ci, then npm run typecheck, test:unit (1179 passed), test:integration (55 passed) and build: all exit 0. A manual mutation (removing the id sort) made the property tests fail, and I restored it.
open_assumptions: Sites are caller-supplied {id, x, y}. Pedestal ids are the caller's ids and positions are not read by the rules.
A player absent from a tick's facts counts as released. A skipped world tick (input.tick > state.tick + 1) interrupts every channel with reason 'gap'.
A refused held request is reported on every tick it is held, not only on its first tick.
Malformed facts (an unknown pedestal id, a duplicate or empty player id, non-boolean flags) throw a RangeError, as stepClaim does, instead of returning a result.
createFruitState takes a 4th optional options argument {tick, rules} beyond the three named in the design.
